note: Differences between the reference service and the Java one that are known. `why` is either a step that is not ported yet, or a row of docs/JAVA-INTENDED-DIFFERENCES.md. `case` names one case (or, ending in *, every case whose name starts so); `path` names what differs (or, ending in *, everything under a prefix: `$.*` is the whole body); `pathMatches` is a pattern instead, for a field of whichever row of a list. `ofSeed` narrows an entry to the object whose `id` is one of these seeded ids (parity/seed.json), `ref` / `java` to these two values. An entry that no longer occurs fails the run, so the list cannot go stale. `audit` lists the audit rows that differ for the same reasons (tools/compare-audit.mjs).

differences.case: attest: *
differences.why: D-08: an inscription is not swept into a batch, and its bundle is available from the start; the reference says so only once its batcher has put the record into a batch

differences.case: attest: a document whose content type does not fit in one push as bytes
differences.why: D-09: a content type of more than 520 bytes is refused as one that does not fit in one push; the reference measures characters (261), accepts it and refuses the document for its size. (With a document under the limit the reference would go on to the wallet with it: the case carries one over the limit, so that neither service can.)

differences.case: attest: a document over the limit, its content type UTF-8 on the wire
differences.why: D-09: the header's 262 bytes are 262 characters, 524 bytes in the script — refused as a content type that does not fit in one push; the reference counts 262 characters, accepts the content type and refuses the document for its size
